content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have moved their children to a new school just two days into the academic year.

According to Hello! magazine, which broke the story first, Prince Archie (5) and Princess Lilibet (3) were withdrawn after their security team raised concerns.

Reports indicate that Harry and Meghan's private security team warned of potential risks to the family, including heavy traffic near the school and lengthy commutes. Hello! also reported that one incident made it difficult for the family's convoy to travel together.

A spokesperson for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex told HuffPost: "The decision to change schools was made after discussing the practical realities of their current arrangements with their family security team."

The spokesperson added: "The parents remain deeply grateful to all the teachers and staff for the care and dedication they have shown their family over the years. This decision should in no way be seen as a reflection of the school, nor the wonderful care their children have received while attending."

Harry previously lost government-funded police protection after stepping back from royal duties, and has since voiced concerns about his security arrangements in the UK.

He has challenged the decision through the courts, arguing that the current arrangements leave him and his family facing significant risk.

Speaking to the BBC in May 2025, while the family was living in the US, he said: "I can't see a world in which I would be bringing my wife and children back to the UK at this point."

The Daily Telegraph reports that, since they are currently residing in the UK, the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (RAVEC) will conduct a new official risk assessment for the couple.
